items.title: Jerry Bergonzi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 7, 2022
items.q: like you were saying Gary Smulyan said you know play what you hear

ctx.x: I’d like to ask more about that but I’m not sure how to ask it. If you’ve got these techniques in your head and then do they become in your hands? Do they happen without you thinking about them?

Well great question. I heard the story that when Miles was playing at the Plugged Nickel the band got together and said, “Let’s play what we don’t hear.” And that doesn’t mean, like you were saying Gary Smulyan said you know play what you hear. They’re not saying that. But there’s certain things that naturally you would play, the first onslaught of ideas. Don’t play those. Wade through it all and get to something in the back there that’s a little different, a little — that’s one thing. So the other thing that I…

Can you imagine being in a situation and you’re improvising and you are distracted. Let’s say you’ve parked your car for wherever this gig is and you think it could be towed away. Do you have a way to not let that kind of interference interfere with you?
